- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast, targeting 1–2 std dev below recent high.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for first 7 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit recent noise; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
